sections.label: B
sections.title: Complete the sentences.
sections.note: Use the word bank: prodigy, sketch, street painter, carpenter, string.

questions.prompt: 1. We watched the ___ draw a horse on the ground.
questions.explanation: A street painter creates pictures in a public place, often on the ground.

questions.prompt: 2. He's only 7 years old and his paintings are amazing! He must be a ___.
questions.explanation: A prodigy is a young person with an exceptional natural ability.

questions.prompt: 3. You need a pencil and a piece of paper to make a ___.
questions.explanation: A sketch is a quick, simple drawing.

questions.prompt: 4. A ___ can build a table and chair for you.
questions.explanation: A carpenter makes or repairs wooden objects.

parts.label: Missing word
parts.explanation: A canvas is the surface an artist paints on.

parts.label: Missing word

sections.label: D
sections.title: Circle the correct words.
sections.note: Choose the word that makes each sentence complete and logical.

questions.prompt: 1. I think that ___ can learn to draw.
questions.explanation: Anyone means any person at all. The sentence says drawing can be learned by every person.

questions.prompt: 2. I can't see ___ because it's too dark.
questions.explanation: Anything is normally used after a negative verb such as can't see.

questions.prompt: 3. ___ in my class is taking a test tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Everyone means all the people in the class.

questions.prompt: 4. I have ___ to do after school.
questions.explanation: Something refers to an unspecified activity or task; someone refers to a person.

questions.prompt: 1. She's at a new school. She doesn't have friends yet because she doesn't know ___ in her class.
questions.explanation: Use anyone or anybody after the negative verb doesn't know.

questions.prompt: 2. I think there is ___ at the door. The doorbell just rang.
questions.explanation: Someone or somebody refers to an unknown person at the door.

questions.prompt: 3. He's bored and can't think of ___ to do.
questions.explanation: Anything is used after can't to refer to an activity of any kind.

questions.prompt: 4. That meal was delicious. I ate ___ on my plate.
questions.explanation: Everything means all the food that was on the plate.

sections.note: Write each complete sentence, then choose picture a, b, or c.

questions.prompt: 1. be / can / artist / an / Anyone

parts.label: Sentence
parts.explanation: The correct order is subject + modal + base verb + complement: Anyone can be an artist.

parts.label: Picture label
parts.explanation: Picture b shows people painting, so it matches sentence 1.

questions.prompt: 2. something / eat / I / to / want

parts.label: Sentence
parts.explanation: Use want + something + to-infinitive: I want something to eat.

parts.label: Picture label
parts.explanation: Picture c shows someone looking for food, so it matches sentence 2.

questions.prompt: 3. party / coming / our / Everyone / is / to

parts.label: Sentence
answers: Everyone is coming to our party
Everyone is coming to our party.
parts.explanation: The present continuous is is coming, followed by to our party.

parts.label: Picture label
parts.explanation: Picture a is a party invitation, so it matches sentence 3.

sections.label: H
sections.title: Look and complete the sentences.
sections.note: Study each clean original illustration and write the art word that completes the sentence.

questions.prompt: 1. In this painting, there is a lot of ___ between light and dark colors.
questions.explanation: Contrast is the clear difference between light and dark areas.

questions.prompt: 2. Different thicknesses of oil paint and paintbrushes created an interesting ___ in this painting.
questions.explanation: Texture is how a surface looks or feels. The different lines and paint thicknesses create a varied texture.

questions.prompt: 3. The artist painted a ___ orange sunrise. The sun was very bright.
questions.explanation: Brilliant means very bright and vivid, which fits the bright orange sunrise.

questions.prompt: 4. The artist used ___ colors to create a calm feeling.
questions.explanation: Pale colors are light and not strong, so they can create a calm feeling.

sections.label: J
sections.title: Write the words in the correct order to make sentences or questions.
sections.note: Use every word once. Add capital letters and punctuation.

questions.prompt: 1. get / I / you / sweater / Shall / a
answers: Shall I get you a sweater
Shall I get you a sweater?
questions.explanation: Use Shall I + base verb to offer help: Shall I get you a sweater?

questions.prompt: 2. help / you / homework / I / your / will / with
answers: I will help you with your homework
I will help you with your homework.
questions.explanation: Use will for a promise or offer: I will help you with your homework.

questions.prompt: 3. take / to / you / store / will / I / the
answers: I will take you to the store
I will take you to the store.
questions.explanation: The correct order is: I will take you to the store.

questions.prompt: 4. turn down / music / Shall / the / I
answers: Shall I turn down the music
Shall I turn down the music?
questions.explanation: Use Shall I + base verb for an offer: Shall I turn down the music?

sections.label: K
sections.title: Complete the sentences. Write will or shall.
sections.note: Use shall in questions that offer help; use will in statements that promise help.

questions.prompt: 1. I ___ give you a call when I get home.
questions.explanation: This is a statement and a promise, so use will.

questions.prompt: 2. ___ I find out what time the museum opens?
questions.explanation: Shall I ...? is used to offer to do something.

questions.prompt: 3. ___ I pick you up from school tomorrow?
questions.explanation: This question offers help, so use Shall I ...?

questions.prompt: 4. I ___ wash the dishes for you.
questions.explanation: This is a statement offering help, so use will.

questions.prompt: 5. I ___ help you clean your room.
questions.explanation: This is a statement and an offer, so use will.

questions.prompt: 6. ___ I make dinner now?
questions.explanation: This is a question offering to make dinner, so use Shall I ...?

sections.note: Write each complete sentence or question, then choose picture a or b.

questions.prompt: 1. glass / I / you / get / Shall / water / of / a

parts.label: Question
answers: Shall I get you a glass of water

parts.explanation: Use Shall I + base verb for an offer: Shall I get you a glass of water?

questions.prompt: 2. open / help / I / you / it / will

parts.explanation: Picture b shows a person helping someone open a container.
